body.text: 9 March 2016

[Research](https://www.ipsos-mori.com/researchpublications/researcharchive/3188/Perceptions-are-not-reality-the-top-10-we-get-wrong.aspx) has found that the British public often have misconceptions about teenage pregnancies.
How far are your perceptions from the truth?
Here we challenge you to test your understanding of the facts about teenage pregnancy in England and Wales.

body.title: Teenage pregnancy â€“ perception versus reality

body.text: Teenage pregnancies since 1969
Now let’s take a look at the teenage pregnancy rate over time.
You might think that teenage pregnancies are a more recent phenomenon but this chart shows that they are not: in fact rates for both under 16s and under 18s have been falling since 2007.

body.text: The fall in teenage pregnancies in recent years is likely to be due to:

body.h4: Percentage of girls under 16 and under 18 becoming pregnant, England and Wales, 1969 to 20141
body.text: initiatives by the government, for example improved sex and relationship guidance and improved access to contraception and sexual health services

body.h4: Percentage of girls under 16 and under 18 becoming pregnant, England and Wales, 1969 to 20141
body.text: more young women in higher education

body.h4: Percentage of girls under 16 and under 18 becoming pregnant, England and Wales, 1969 to 20141
body.text: negative attitudes towards teenage mothers in society

body.h4: Percentage of girls under 16 and under 18 becoming pregnant, England and Wales, 1969 to 20141
body.text: Governments in both England and Wales are committed to reducing the teenage pregnancy rate further, although they have now moved away from setting specific targets.

body.h4: Percentage of girls under 16 and under 18 becoming pregnant, England and Wales, 1969 to 20141
body.text: The[last target](http://webarchive.nationalarchives.gov.uk/20091212133529/http://dcsf.gov.uk/everychildmatters/healthandwellbeing/teenagepregnancy/about/strategy/), set by the government in England in 1999, was to halve the 1998 under 18 teenage pregnancy rate for England by 2010. Rates fell substantially during this period and this target was [reached in 2014](https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/birthsdeathsandmarriages/conceptionandfertilityrates/bulletins/conceptionstatistics/previousReleases).
